title: "Information Gain Propagation: A New Way to Graph Active Learning with Soft Labels"

en.text: Graph neural networks (GNNs) are strong at tasks like node classification, but that strength comes with a bill: they need a lot of labeled nodes, and human annotation is slow and expensive. Active learning is the usual way to cut that bill. Instead of labeling blindly, each round picks the nodes most worth labeling and sends only those to an expert. Yet no matter how clever the selection strategy is, almost every prior graph active-learning method rests on the same unspoken assumption: that an expert can always name the exact class a node belongs to.

That assumption breaks down when the label space is large or the domain is unfamiliar. Take ogbn-papers100M from the Open Graph Benchmark, which has 172 classes. Asking an annotator to pinpoint the exact class of a node out of a hundred-plus candidates is beyond what most people can do reliably, and the labeling budget gets spent on questions that are simply too hard to answer well.

This ICLR 2022 paper takes a different route. Rather than asking "which class does it belong to?", it asks a much cheaper binary question: "does it belong to the (model's guessed) first category, yes or no?" This relaxed query does not return an exact class; it returns a soft label. Paired with it is a new selection criterion that deliberately picks the nodes whose information gain propagates farthest across the graph. The result: higher accuracy at the same labeling cost.

en.caption: Figure 1. Two labeling strategies. Top, the paper's relaxed query: given the model's prediction (0.5/0.3/0.2), the oracle only answers "does it belong to the first category?", and the yes/no reply becomes a normalized soft label (yes -> 1/0/0, no -> 0/0.6/0.4). Bottom, prior work: the oracle must name the exact ground-truth class. The binary question on the left is plainly easier to answer than the multi-class question on the right.

en.text: Paper: Information Gain Propagation: A New Way to Graph Active Learning with Soft Labels (ICLR 2022, arXiv:2203.01093, https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.01093). The authors are from Peking University and Apple.
The problem: the expensive part is also the wrong question

Break the labeling cost apart and two long-overlooked sources of waste appear. The first is the cost of the query itself. Asking an expert to identify the exact class among c categories is roughly c-1 times as demanding, and as expensive, as answering a single binary question, and the gap grows with the number of classes. Prior methods implicitly treat one exact annotation as the atomic unit of cost, so their budgets are inflated from the start.

The second is the narrow view of the selection criterion. Most prior criteria were designed for hard labels and measure only the uncertainty of a single node in isolation. They ignore a defining property of GNNs: labeling one node propagates supervision along the graph to its k-hop neighbors. A node's real value is therefore not just how uncertain it is on its own, but how much of its neighborhood it can illuminate.
The method: let information gain propagate through the graph

IGP (Information Gain Propagation) folds both ideas into a single loop. The pipeline cycles through three stages: train a GNN on the currently labeled nodes using their soft labels (Model Training); pick the nodes most worth labeling this round with the new criterion (Node Selection); and issue relaxed queries on the chosen nodes, turning each yes/no answer into a normalized soft label before updating the data (Node Labeling). Then it repeats.

en.caption: Figure 3. Overview of the IGP framework. Left: a GNN is trained on the labeled set V_l with soft labels. Center: selection combines each node's Influence Magnitude with its Information Gain, whose product is the Propagated Information Gain. Right: relaxed queries on the selected set V_b yield normalized soft labels, which feed back to update the model.

en.text: The selection criterion is the heart of IGP and where it parts ways with earlier work. For each candidate node, IGP does not just ask how much labeling it would reduce that node's own uncertainty; it asks how much uncertainty would fall across every node in its receptive field once the label propagates. Concretely, it estimates a node's influence magnitude on its neighbors via feature-gradient / random-walk propagation over a k-layer GNN, then weights each influenced node's information gain, its drop in entropy, by that influence. Summing the product over the receptive field gives the node's information-gain-propagation score.

Selection then becomes a budget-constrained maximization: within a labeling budget B, choose the subset of nodes that maximizes the total propagated information gain across the graph. In plain terms, IGP does not pick the node that is most confused about itself; it picks the node whose single label lights up the most of its neighborhood.
Results: a consistent lead across five datasets and four backbones

The authors evaluate on five standard graph benchmarks: the citation networks Cora, Citeseer, and PubMed, the large social network Reddit, and ogbn-arxiv from the Open Graph Benchmark. Crucially, the budget is not counted as the number of nodes labeled but as the true annotation cost, since an exact multi-class query is c-1 times more expensive than a binary one. Under an equal budget of 20 labels per class with a GCN backbone, IGP reaches the highest accuracy on all five datasets.

en.caption: Table 1. Test accuracy (%) under an equal labeling budget (20 labels per class, GCN backbone). Against the strongest baseline, GRAIN, IGP gains 1.6-2.2% on the citation networks, +0.9% on Reddit, and +0.6% on ogbn-arxiv.

en.text: More telling than any single number is how accuracy scales with budget. As the labeling budget grows, IGP's accuracy climbs the fastest and stays ahead at every budget point. The advantage is not an artifact of one lucky budget setting; it holds across the whole curve.

en.caption: Figure 4. Test accuracy as the labeling budget grows (citation network, GCN). The top pink curve is IGP: it leads from the smallest budget onward, and the margin over the other active-learning baselines widens as the budget increases.

en.text: The lead is robust to the choice of backbone as well. On PubMed, across SGC, APPNP, GCN, and MVGRL, IGP beats both ALG and GRAIN by more than 1.8%, which suggests the payoff from relaxed queries plus propagation-aware selection does not hinge on any one network architecture.
Why it works: more spread-out selections, and every piece pulls its weight

What makes IGP stronger? One intuition comes from where its chosen nodes land on the graph. Projecting the nodes IGP selects on Cora to two dimensions with t-SNE shows them spread fairly evenly across the embedding space rather than clustering in a few regions. A propagation-aware criterion naturally favors nodes whose influence covers different neighborhoods, so the resulting labeled set is more representative and less redundant.

en.caption: Figure 5. t-SNE distribution of the nodes IGP selects on Cora. Colored points are the selected nodes; gray points are all nodes. The selections spread across the entire embedding space, covering distinct regions, which reflects the diversity and representativeness of the selection.

en.text: An ablation confirms that each component earns its place: removing any one of them costs accuracy. Dropping the propagation-aware selection (informative selection) hurts most, up to -3.2% on PubMed and -2.5% on Cora, making it the single most important ingredient. Removing soft-label training (informative training) costs up to -2.9%, dropping the influence magnitude (information quantity) up to -2.1%, and removing the normalized soft label up to -2.4%. The reading is clear: what really separates IGP from the pack is propagation-aware selection, not simply the switch to soft labels.
Takeaway: change the question, and change how you choose

IGP's recipe is compact: replace the expensive exact-class annotation with a cheap binary yes/no that yields a soft label, and replace the "who is most uncertain" selection rule with "whose information gain propagates farthest across the graph." Together they make graph active learning both more accurate and cheaper to label at an equal cost, and the recipe drops onto any GNN backbone.

It is worth being honest about the boundaries. The soft label is built from the model's current prediction plus a single binary confirmation from the oracle, so its quality depends on how good that prediction distribution is; the cost advantage rests on the assumption that a binary query really is c-1 times cheaper than a multi-class one, and the actual savings will vary with the task and the annotation setup. Still, as a plug-in paradigm, relaxed queries plus propagation-aware selection point graph active learning in a direction worth pursuing.

zh.text: 图神经网络（Graph Neural Network, GNN）在节点分类等任务上表现很强，但代价是需要大量带标签的节点，而人工标注既慢又贵。主动学习（active learning）本是缓解这一问题的常规做法：不盲目标注，而是每一轮只挑出最值得标注的节点交给专家。可无论选点策略多聪明，过去几乎所有图主动学习方法都建立在同一个隐含假设上——专家总能一口报出某个节点确切属于哪一类。
问题在于，当类别数很大或领域比较陌生时，这个假设并不成立。以 OGB 里的 ogbn-papers100M 为例，它有 172 个类别；要专家从上百个候选类里精确指出一个节点的确切类别，远超一般标注者的能力，标注预算就在这种高难度的问题上被大量浪费。
这篇 ICLR 2022 的工作换了个思路：与其问「它到底属于哪一类」，不如只问一个便宜得多的二元问题——「它属于（模型猜的）第一类吗？是或否」。这个被放松（relaxed）后的查询给出的不是精确类别，而是一个软标签（soft label）；配套的一个新选点准则，则专门去挑那些「信息增益能沿着图传得最远」的节点。结果是：在同样的标注成本下，精度更高。

zh.caption: 图1 两种标注策略的对比。上方是本文的放松查询：面对模型预测（0.5/0.3/0.2），只问「是否属于第一类」，专家回答「是/否」即可，答案被转成归一化的软标签（如「是」→1/0/0，「否」→0/0.6/0.4）。下方是以往方法：必须让专家直接说出确切类别（ground truth label）。左边的二元问题显然比右边的多分类问题更容易回答。

zh.text: 论文：Information Gain Propagation: A New Way to Graph Active Learning with Soft Labels（ICLR 2022，arXiv:2203.01093，https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.01093）。作者来自北京大学与 Apple。
问题：贵的不只是标注，还有「问错了问题」
把标注成本拆开看，会发现两个一直被忽略的浪费点。第一是查询本身的成本：让专家在 c 个类别里指认确切类别，难度和花费大约是回答一个二元问题的 c−1 倍；类别越多，这个差距越大。以往方法却默认「一次精确标注」是最小的成本单位，于是预算天然被高估。
第二是选点准则的视野。以往准则大多沿用为硬标签（hard label）设计的思路，只衡量单个节点自身的不确定性（uncertainty），却忽略了 GNN 的一个本质特性：标注一个节点，监督信号会顺着图结构传播到它的 k 跳邻居。也就是说，一个节点的价值不该只看它自己，而要看它能把信息「照亮」多大一片邻域。
方法：让信息增益沿着图传播
IGP（Information Gain Propagation）把上面两点合到一个闭环里。整个流程在三步之间循环：先用当前已标注节点的软标签训练 GNN（Model Training）；再按新准则挑出这一轮最该标注的节点（Node Selection）；最后对选中的节点发起放松查询，把「是/否」答案转成归一化软标签并更新数据（Node Labeling），如此往复。

zh.caption: 图3 IGP 框架总览。左：用软标签在已标注节点集 V_l 上训练 GNN；中：选点时同时考虑「影响力大小（Influence Magnitude）」与「信息增益（Information Gain）」，二者相乘得到「传播后的信息增益（Propagated Information Gain）」；右：对选中节点 V_b 发起放松查询，得到归一化软标签，再回到左侧更新模型。

zh.text: 选点准则是 IGP 的核心，也是它和以往方法拉开差距的地方。对每个候选节点，IGP 不只问「标它能减少它自己多少不确定性」，而是问「标它之后，它的整个感受野（receptive field）里所有被影响到的节点，加起来能减少多少不确定性」。具体做法分两块：用特征梯度 / 随机游走在 k 层 GNN 上估计一个节点对邻居的影响力大小，再用这个影响力去加权每个被影响节点的信息增益（即熵的下降）。二者的乘积在感受野上求和，就是这个节点的「信息增益传播」值。
于是选点变成一个带预算约束的最大化问题：在标注预算 B 之内，选出使全图传播信息增益之和最大的节点子集。换句话说，IGP 挑的不是「自己最迷糊」的节点，而是「一标下去、能顺着图照亮最多邻居」的节点。
结果：五个数据集、四种骨干网络上的稳定领先
作者在五个标准图基准上评测：三个引文网络 Cora、Citeseer、PubMed，一个大规模社交网络 Reddit，以及 OGB 的 ogbn-arxiv。关键的一点是，预算不再按「标了多少个节点」计，而是按真实的标注成本（金钱）来算——毕竟一个精确多分类查询要比一个二元查询贵 c−1 倍。在每类 20 个标注的同等预算、GCN 骨干下，IGP 在全部五个数据集上都取得最高精度。

zh.caption: 表1 同等标注预算（每类 20 个标注，GCN 骨干）下的测试精度（%）。IGP 相比最强基线 GRAIN，在三个引文网络上提升 1.6–2.2%，在 Reddit 上 +0.9%，在 ogbn-arxiv 上 +0.6%。

zh.text: 更值得注意的是精度随预算增长的曲线。当标注预算逐步增大时，IGP 的精度爬升得最快，并在每一个预算点上都保持领先——这说明它的优势不是靠某个特定预算「刚好卡对」，而是在整条曲线上都成立。

zh.caption: 图4 测试精度随标注预算变化的曲线（引文网络，GCN）。最上方的粉色曲线为 IGP：从最小预算起就领先，且随预算增大，与其他主动学习基线的差距进一步拉开。

zh.text: 这种领先在不同 GNN 骨干上同样稳健。在 PubMed 上，横跨 SGC、APPNP、GCN、MVGRL 四种骨干，IGP 比 ALG 和 GRAIN 都高出 1.8% 以上，说明「放松查询 + 传播感知选点」的收益并不依赖某一种特定网络结构。
为什么有效：选点更分散，拆掉哪块都会掉分
IGP 为什么更强？一个直观的解释来自它选出的节点在图上的分布。把 Cora 上被选中的节点用 t-SNE 投到二维平面，可以看到它们相当均匀地散布在整个嵌入空间里，而不是扎堆在少数几个区域。传播感知的准则天然偏好那些影响力能覆盖不同邻域的节点，因此选出的标注集更有代表性、冗余更少。

zh.caption: 图5 IGP 在 Cora 上所选节点的 t-SNE 分布。彩色点为被选中标注的节点，灰色点为全体节点；被选中的节点铺满整个嵌入空间，覆盖各个区域，体现出选点的多样性与代表性。

zh.text: 消融实验进一步印证了每个部件的作用：逐一去掉一个组件都会掉分。去掉传播感知的选点（informative selection）损失最大，PubMed 上最多掉 3.2%、Cora 上掉 2.5%，是最关键的一环；去掉软标签训练（informative training）最多掉 2.9%，去掉影响力大小（information quantity）最多掉 2.1%，去掉归一化软标签（normalized label）最多掉 2.4%。这也说明：真正把 IGP 和别人拉开的，是「传播感知的选点」，而不仅仅是换用软标签。
小结：换个问法，也换个选法
IGP 的配方其实很简洁：把昂贵的「精确多分类」标注，换成一个便宜的二元 yes/no 问题得到软标签；再把选点准则从「谁最不确定」换成「谁的信息增益能沿图传得最远」。两者叠加，让图主动学习在同等标注成本下既更准、又更省，而且这套思路可以接在任意 GNN 骨干之上。
当然也要看清它的边界：软标签由「模型预测 + 专家的一次二元确认」构造，其质量依赖模型当前的预测分布；成本上的优势建立在「二元查询确实比多分类便宜 c−1 倍」这一假设之上，实际收益会随任务和标注方式而变化。但作为一个可插拔的通用范式，「放松查询 + 传播感知选点」给图主动学习指出了一个值得继续走下去的方向。

于是选点变成一个带预算约束的最大化问题：在标注预算 B 之内，选出使全图传播信息增益之和最大的节点子集。换句话说，IGP 挑的不是「自己最迷糊」的节点，而是「一标下去、能顺着图照亮最多邻居」的节点。

en.text: The method: let information gain propagate through the graph

IGP (Information Gain Propagation) folds both ideas into a single loop. The pipeline cycles through three stages: train a GNN on the currently labeled nodes using their soft labels (Model Training); pick the nodes most worth labeling this round with the new criterion (Node Selection); and issue relaxed queries on the chosen nodes, turning each yes/no answer into a normalized soft label before updating the data (Node Labeling). Then it repeats.

en.caption: Figure 3. Overview of the IGP framework. Left: a GNN is trained on the labeled set V_l with soft labels. Center: selection combines each node's Influence Magnitude with its Information Gain, whose product is the Propagated Information Gain. Right: relaxed queries on the selected set V_b yield normalized soft labels, which feed back to update the model.

en.text: The selection criterion is the heart of IGP and where it parts ways with earlier work. For each candidate node, IGP does not just ask how much labeling it would reduce that node's own uncertainty; it asks how much uncertainty would fall across every node in its receptive field once the label propagates. Concretely, it estimates a node's influence magnitude on its neighbors via feature-gradient / random-walk propagation over a k-layer GNN, then weights each influenced node's information gain, its drop in entropy, by that influence. Summing the product over the receptive field gives the node's information-gain-propagation score.

Selection then becomes a budget-constrained maximization: within a labeling budget B, choose the subset of nodes that maximizes the total propagated information gain across the graph. In plain terms, IGP does not pick the node that is most confused about itself; it picks the node whose single label lights up the most of its neighborhood.

zh.title: ICLR 2022 | 别再问节点属于哪一类：换个更便宜的问法，图主动学习又准又省
zh.subtitle: 北京大学与 Apple 提出 IGP：用二元查询和软标签，重新定义图神经网络的主动学习

en.text: Graph neural networks (GNNs) are strong at tasks like node classification, but that strength comes with a bill: they need a lot of labeled nodes, and human annotation is slow and expensive. Active learning is the usual way to cut that bill. Instead of labeling blindly, each round picks the nodes most worth labeling and sends only those to an expert. Yet no matter how clever the selection strategy is, almost every prior graph active-learning method rests on the same unspoken assumption: that an expert can always name the exact class a node belongs to.

That assumption breaks down when the label space is large or the domain is unfamiliar. Take ogbn-papers100M from the Open Graph Benchmark, which has 172 classes. Asking an annotator to pinpoint the exact class of a node out of a hundred-plus candidates is beyond what most people can do reliably, and the labeling budget gets spent on questions that are simply too hard to answer well.

This ICLR 2022 paper takes a different route. Rather than asking "which class does it belong to?", it asks a much cheaper binary question: "does it belong to the (model's guessed) first category, yes or no?" This relaxed query does not return an exact class; it returns a soft label. Paired with it is a new selection criterion that deliberately picks the nodes whose information gain propagates farthest across the graph. The result: higher accuracy at the same labeling cost.

en.caption: Figure 1. Two labeling strategies. Top, the paper's relaxed query: given the model's prediction (0.5/0.3/0.2), the oracle only answers "does it belong to the first category?", and the yes/no reply becomes a normalized soft label (yes -> 1/0/0, no -> 0/0.6/0.4). Bottom, prior work: the oracle must name the exact ground-truth class. The binary question on the left is plainly easier to answer than the multi-class question on the right.

en.text: Paper: Information Gain Propagation: A New Way to Graph Active Learning with Soft Labels (ICLR 2022, arXiv:2203.01093, https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.01093). The authors are from Peking University and Apple.
The problem: the expensive part is also the wrong question

Break the labeling cost apart and two long-overlooked sources of waste appear. The first is the cost of the query itself. Asking an expert to identify the exact class among c categories is roughly c-1 times as demanding, and as expensive, as answering a single binary question, and the gap grows with the number of classes. Prior methods implicitly treat one exact annotation as the atomic unit of cost, so their budgets are inflated from the start.

The second is the narrow view of the selection criterion. Most prior criteria were designed for hard labels and measure only the uncertainty of a single node in isolation. They ignore a defining property of GNNs: labeling one node propagates supervision along the graph to its k-hop neighbors. A node's real value is therefore not just how uncertain it is on its own, but how much of its neighborhood it can illuminate.

zh.text: 图神经网络（Graph Neural Network, GNN）在节点分类等任务上表现很强，但代价是需要大量带标签的节点，而人工标注既慢又贵。主动学习（active learning）本是缓解这一问题的常规做法：不盲目标注，而是每一轮只挑出最值得标注的节点交给专家。可无论选点策略多聪明，过去几乎所有图主动学习方法都建立在同一个隐含假设上——专家总能一口报出某个节点确切属于哪一类。
问题在于，当类别数很大或领域比较陌生时，这个假设并不成立。以 OGB 里的 ogbn-papers100M 为例，它有 172 个类别；要专家从上百个候选类里精确指出一个节点的确切类别，远超一般标注者的能力，标注预算就在这种高难度的问题上被大量浪费。
这篇 ICLR 2022 的工作换了个思路：与其问「它到底属于哪一类」，不如只问一个便宜得多的二元问题——「它属于（模型猜的）第一类吗？是或否」。这个被放松（relaxed）后的查询给出的不是精确类别，而是一个软标签（soft label）；配套的一个新选点准则，则专门去挑那些「信息增益能沿着图传得最远」的节点。结果是：在同样的标注成本下，精度更高。

zh.caption: 图1 两种标注策略的对比。上方是本文的放松查询：面对模型预测（0.5/0.3/0.2），只问「是否属于第一类」，专家回答「是/否」即可，答案被转成归一化的软标签（如「是」→1/0/0，「否」→0/0.6/0.4）。下方是以往方法：必须让专家直接说出确切类别（ground truth label）。左边的二元问题显然比右边的多分类问题更容易回答。

zh.text: 论文：Information Gain Propagation: A New Way to Graph Active Learning with Soft Labels（ICLR 2022，arXiv:2203.01093，https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.01093）。作者来自北京大学与 Apple。
问题：贵的不只是标注，还有「问错了问题」
把标注成本拆开看，会发现两个一直被忽略的浪费点。第一是查询本身的成本：让专家在 c 个类别里指认确切类别，难度和花费大约是回答一个二元问题的 c−1 倍；类别越多，这个差距越大。以往方法却默认「一次精确标注」是最小的成本单位，于是预算天然被高估。
第二是选点准则的视野。以往准则大多沿用为硬标签（hard label）设计的思路，只衡量单个节点自身的不确定性（uncertainty），却忽略了 GNN 的一个本质特性：标注一个节点，监督信号会顺着图结构传播到它的 k 跳邻居。也就是说，一个节点的价值不该只看它自己，而要看它能把信息「照亮」多大一片邻域。

en.title: Stop Asking Which Class a Node Belongs To: A Cheaper Question Makes Graph Active Learning Both Better and Cheaper
en.subtitle: Peking University and Apple introduce IGP, rethinking active learning for graph neural networks with relaxed queries and soft labels

zh.title: ICLR 2022 | 别再问节点属于哪一类：换个更便宜的问法，图主动学习又准又省
zh.subtitle: 北京大学与 Apple 提出 IGP：用二元查询和软标签，重新定义图神经网络的主动学习

en.text: Results: a consistent lead across five datasets and four backbones

The authors evaluate on five standard graph benchmarks: the citation networks Cora, Citeseer, and PubMed, the large social network Reddit, and ogbn-arxiv from the Open Graph Benchmark. Crucially, the budget is not counted as the number of nodes labeled but as the true annotation cost, since an exact multi-class query is c-1 times more expensive than a binary one. Under an equal budget of 20 labels per class with a GCN backbone, IGP reaches the highest accuracy on all five datasets.

en.caption: Table 1. Test accuracy (%) under an equal labeling budget (20 labels per class, GCN backbone). Against the strongest baseline, GRAIN, IGP gains 1.6-2.2% on the citation networks, +0.9% on Reddit, and +0.6% on ogbn-arxiv.

en.text: More telling than any single number is how accuracy scales with budget. As the labeling budget grows, IGP's accuracy climbs the fastest and stays ahead at every budget point. The advantage is not an artifact of one lucky budget setting; it holds across the whole curve.

en.caption: Figure 4. Test accuracy as the labeling budget grows (citation network, GCN). The top pink curve is IGP: it leads from the smallest budget onward, and the margin over the other active-learning baselines widens as the budget increases.

en.text: The lead is robust to the choice of backbone as well. On PubMed, across SGC, APPNP, GCN, and MVGRL, IGP beats both ALG and GRAIN by more than 1.8%, which suggests the payoff from relaxed queries plus propagation-aware selection does not hinge on any one network architecture.

zh.text: 结果：五个数据集、四种骨干网络上的稳定领先
作者在五个标准图基准上评测：三个引文网络 Cora、Citeseer、PubMed，一个大规模社交网络 Reddit，以及 OGB 的 ogbn-arxiv。关键的一点是，预算不再按「标了多少个节点」计，而是按真实的标注成本（金钱）来算——毕竟一个精确多分类查询要比一个二元查询贵 c−1 倍。在每类 20 个标注的同等预算、GCN 骨干下，IGP 在全部五个数据集上都取得最高精度。

zh.caption: 表1 同等标注预算（每类 20 个标注，GCN 骨干）下的测试精度（%）。IGP 相比最强基线 GRAIN，在三个引文网络上提升 1.6–2.2%，在 Reddit 上 +0.9%，在 ogbn-arxiv 上 +0.6%。

zh.text: 更值得注意的是精度随预算增长的曲线。当标注预算逐步增大时，IGP 的精度爬升得最快，并在每一个预算点上都保持领先——这说明它的优势不是靠某个特定预算「刚好卡对」，而是在整条曲线上都成立。

zh.caption: 图4 测试精度随标注预算变化的曲线（引文网络，GCN）。最上方的粉色曲线为 IGP：从最小预算起就领先，且随预算增大，与其他主动学习基线的差距进一步拉开。

zh.text: 这种领先在不同 GNN 骨干上同样稳健。在 PubMed 上，横跨 SGC、APPNP、GCN、MVGRL 四种骨干，IGP 比 ALG 和 GRAIN 都高出 1.8% 以上，说明「放松查询 + 传播感知选点」的收益并不依赖某一种特定网络结构。

zh.title: ICLR 2022 | 别再问节点属于哪一类：换个更便宜的问法，图主动学习又准又省
zh.subtitle: 北京大学与 Apple 提出 IGP：用二元查询和软标签，重新定义图神经网络的主动学习

en.text: Why it works: more spread-out selections, and every piece pulls its weight

What makes IGP stronger? One intuition comes from where its chosen nodes land on the graph. Projecting the nodes IGP selects on Cora to two dimensions with t-SNE shows them spread fairly evenly across the embedding space rather than clustering in a few regions. A propagation-aware criterion naturally favors nodes whose influence covers different neighborhoods, so the resulting labeled set is more representative and less redundant.

en.caption: Figure 5. t-SNE distribution of the nodes IGP selects on Cora. Colored points are the selected nodes; gray points are all nodes. The selections spread across the entire embedding space, covering distinct regions, which reflects the diversity and representativeness of the selection.

en.text: An ablation confirms that each component earns its place: removing any one of them costs accuracy. Dropping the propagation-aware selection (informative selection) hurts most, up to -3.2% on PubMed and -2.5% on Cora, making it the single most important ingredient. Removing soft-label training (informative training) costs up to -2.9%, dropping the influence magnitude (information quantity) up to -2.1%, and removing the normalized soft label up to -2.4%. The reading is clear: what really separates IGP from the pack is propagation-aware selection, not simply the switch to soft labels.

zh.text: 为什么有效：选点更分散，拆掉哪块都会掉分
IGP 为什么更强？一个直观的解释来自它选出的节点在图上的分布。把 Cora 上被选中的节点用 t-SNE 投到二维平面，可以看到它们相当均匀地散布在整个嵌入空间里，而不是扎堆在少数几个区域。传播感知的准则天然偏好那些影响力能覆盖不同邻域的节点，因此选出的标注集更有代表性、冗余更少。

zh.caption: 图5 IGP 在 Cora 上所选节点的 t-SNE 分布。彩色点为被选中标注的节点，灰色点为全体节点；被选中的节点铺满整个嵌入空间，覆盖各个区域，体现出选点的多样性与代表性。

zh.text: 消融实验进一步印证了每个部件的作用：逐一去掉一个组件都会掉分。去掉传播感知的选点（informative selection）损失最大，PubMed 上最多掉 3.2%、Cora 上掉 2.5%，是最关键的一环；去掉软标签训练（informative training）最多掉 2.9%，去掉影响力大小（information quantity）最多掉 2.1%，去掉归一化软标签（normalized label）最多掉 2.4%。这也说明：真正把 IGP 和别人拉开的，是「传播感知的选点」，而不仅仅是换用软标签。

zh.title: ICLR 2022 | 别再问节点属于哪一类：换个更便宜的问法，图主动学习又准又省
zh.subtitle: 北京大学与 Apple 提出 IGP：用二元查询和软标签，重新定义图神经网络的主动学习

en.text: Results: a consistent lead across five datasets and four backbones

The authors evaluate on five standard graph benchmarks: the citation networks Cora, Citeseer, and PubMed, the large social network Reddit, and ogbn-arxiv from the Open Graph Benchmark. Crucially, the budget is not counted as the number of nodes labeled but as the true annotation cost, since an exact multi-class query is c-1 times more expensive than a binary one. Under an equal budget of 20 labels per class with a GCN backbone, IGP reaches the highest accuracy on all five datasets.

en.caption: Table 1. Test accuracy (%) under an equal labeling budget (20 labels per class, GCN backbone). Against the strongest baseline, GRAIN, IGP gains 1.6-2.2% on the citation networks, +0.9% on Reddit, and +0.6% on ogbn-arxiv.

en.text: More telling than any single number is how accuracy scales with budget. As the labeling budget grows, IGP's accuracy climbs the fastest and stays ahead at every budget point. The advantage is not an artifact of one lucky budget setting; it holds across the whole curve.

en.caption: Figure 4. Test accuracy as the labeling budget grows (citation network, GCN). The top pink curve is IGP: it leads from the smallest budget onward, and the margin over the other active-learning baselines widens as the budget increases.

en.text: The lead is robust to the choice of backbone as well. On PubMed, across SGC, APPNP, GCN, and MVGRL, IGP beats both ALG and GRAIN by more than 1.8%, which suggests the payoff from relaxed queries plus propagation-aware selection does not hinge on any one network architecture.

zh.caption: 图1 两种标注策略的对比。上方是本文的放松查询：面对模型预测（0.5/0.3/0.2），只问「是否属于第一类」，专家回答「是/否」即可，答案被转成归一化的软标签（如「是」→1/0/0，「否」→0/0.6/0.4）。下方是以往方法：必须让专家直接说出确切类别（ground truth label）。左边的二元问题显然比右边的多分类问题更容易回答。

zh.text: 小结：换个问法，也换个选法
IGP 的配方其实很简洁：把昂贵的「精确多分类」标注，换成一个便宜的二元 yes/no 问题得到软标签；再把选点准则从「谁最不确定」换成「谁的信息增益能沿图传得最远」。两者叠加，让图主动学习在同等标注成本下既更准、又更省，而且这套思路可以接在任意 GNN 骨干之上。
当然也要看清它的边界：软标签由「模型预测 + 专家的一次二元确认」构造，其质量依赖模型当前的预测分布；成本上的优势建立在「二元查询确实比多分类便宜 c−1 倍」这一假设之上，实际收益会随任务和标注方式而变化。但作为一个可插拔的通用范式，「放松查询 + 传播感知选点」给图主动学习指出了一个值得继续走下去的方向。

en.caption: Figure 1. Two labeling strategies. Top, the paper's relaxed query: given the model's prediction (0.5/0.3/0.2), the oracle only answers "does it belong to the first category?", and the yes/no reply becomes a normalized soft label (yes -> 1/0/0, no -> 0/0.6/0.4). Bottom, prior work: the oracle must name the exact ground-truth class. The binary question on the left is plainly easier to answer than the multi-class question on the right.

en.text: Takeaway: change the question, and change how you choose

IGP's recipe is compact: replace the expensive exact-class annotation with a cheap binary yes/no that yields a soft label, and replace the "who is most uncertain" selection rule with "whose information gain propagates farthest across the graph." Together they make graph active learning both more accurate and cheaper to label at an equal cost, and the recipe drops onto any GNN backbone.

It is worth being honest about the boundaries. The soft label is built from the model's current prediction plus a single binary confirmation from the oracle, so its quality depends on how good that prediction distribution is; the cost advantage rests on the assumption that a binary query really is c-1 times cheaper than a multi-class one, and the actual savings will vary with the task and the annotation setup. Still, as a plug-in paradigm, relaxed queries plus propagation-aware selection point graph active learning in a direction worth pursuing.
